0.content: Neuvillette is the Hydro Dragon, one of the Seven Sovereigns who ruled the elements before the Heavenly Principles came. Those "usurpers" took the dragons' authority and gave it to The Seven; his was locked in the Hydro Archon's divine throne. He was born in human form, with most of his memories and power lost, not knowing why. In 4.1, when sudden rain fell after the Primordial Sea broke into the Fortress of Meropide, the Traveler guessed the truth. He confirmed it and asked them to keep it secret. When the throne was destroyed in 4.2, he "reforged the throne and title of a Fully Fledged Dragon".

1.comment: Neuvillette: Focalors, Furina and the Seat in the Theater
1.content: Focalors invited Neuvillette to Fontaine with a letter and, he later learned, arranged for him to be Iudex so that living among humans would teach him to feel as they do. For five centuries she hid inside the Oratrice, storing up Indemnitium, while her human half Furina played the Hydro Archon without knowing the plan. In 4.2 Neuvillette put Furina on trial and found her guilty; the Oratrice then sentenced "the Hydro Archon" to death. In a vision Focalors explained everything: the sentence would destroy the divine throne and return his authority. "Hydro Dragon, Hydro Dragon, don't cry," she teased. She was executed, and he declared, "People of Fontaine, your sins are forgiven."

2.content: Neuvillette brought Melusines, whom many Fontainians once saw as omens of calamity, into society and the Marechaussee Phantom, and contributed this article to the legal code: "A Melusine shall be addressed as 'she,' rather than 'it,' for they are people too." To them he is the ideal father. Asked why the dragon gave them human rights, he says, "It wasn't up to me. Melusines simply prefer being around humans, that's all." Melusines staff the Palais Mermonia, including his aide Sedene.

3.content: A little over four hundred years ago, the new Iudex began reforms and brought Melusines, including Carole, to the Court at their request. His two most trusted subordinates were Carole and Vautrin, head of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol. Conservatives who opposed the reforms used Carole's identity to stir up unrest and force him to give up power. Carole took her own life to prove her innocence, and Vautrin took revenge on those responsible. Neuvillette sentenced him to the Fortress of Meropide. Ever since, he has handled Melusine cases with special care.

4.content: Callas, founder of the Spina di Rosula, was framed for murder and died in a court duel against Clorinde. Neuvillette suspected his innocence but did not stop the duel, expecting Callas to yield. In 4.0 he apologised to Navia, who rejected him as insincere, and it rained as she left. They have since exchanged apologies, but he still feels "very distant from her, as if I'm observing the starry sky from the bottom of a deep lake", and knows it cannot easily be mended.

5.content: He met the Traveler as a defence advocate in Lyney's trial (4.0) and came to rely on them as someone with no ties to Fontaine's factions. In 4.2 he made them his "executor" in place of the broken Oratrice and shared the ancient dragons' power with them to defeat the All-Devouring Narwhal. He invites them, as one "from beyond the stars", to witness his judgment of "this upended world" and says travelling with them changed his views.
